### Factual Award Counts

* **Regular-Season MVPs**:
  * **Michael Jordan**: 5 (1987–88, 1990–91, 1991–92, 1995–96, 1997–98) [T1, jordan_accolades_80]
  * **LeBron James**: 4 (2008–09, 2009–10, 2011–12, 2012–13) [T2, lebron_accolades_160]
  * *Comparison*: Jordan leads by 1 regular-season MVP [T1, T2].

* **Finals MVPs**:
  * **Michael Jordan**: 6 (1990–91, 1991–92, 1992–93, 1995–96, 1996–97, 1997–98) [T1, jordan_accolades_80]
  * **LeBron James**: 4 [T2]
  * *Comparison*: Jordan leads by 2 Finals MVPs [T1, T2].

---

### Tradeoffs and Accolade Context

* **Peak Accolade Dominance**: Jordan converted all 6 of his NBA championship runs into Finals MVP awards and captured 5 regular-season MVPs alongside 10 scoring titles [T1, jordan_accolades_80].
* **Longevity and All-NBA Selections**: While trailing Jordan in MVP and Finals MVP honors, LeBron has accumulated more total All-NBA First Team selections (13 compared to Jordan's 10) as well as more total All-NBA selections (21 total across 1st, 2nd, and 3rd teams, compared to Jordan's 11) [T1, T2, lebron_accolades_160].

---

### Subjective GOAT Judgments vs. Factual Evidence

Factually, Jordan holds higher totals in both regular-season MVPs (5 to 4) and Finals MVPs (6 to 4) [T1, T2]. Determining how these counts factor into a "Greatest of All Time" (GOAT) evaluation is subjective:
* Proponents of Jordan prioritize his higher rate of peak individual trophies and undefeated Finals MVP record (6-for-6) [T1, jordan_accolades_80].
* Proponents of LeBron place greater weight on career longevity, sustained elite play, and a broader accumulation of All-NBA team honors over two decades [T2, lebron_accolades_160].
